q: 1. If TL is the latest allowable event occurrence time, total activity slacks (S), is equal to
explain: Total float/slack can be equivalently computed as LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or TL-EFT, all giving the same result - so all of the above is correct.

q: 2. In PERT, the most likely time is
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: The most likely time ($t_m$) is the duration that would occur most frequently if the activity were repeated many times.

q: 3. All the following are valid for CPM except
options: the beginning and end of an activity is denoted by nodes
explain: CPM assumes deterministic, certain activity durations; allowing uncertainties is NOT valid for CPM (that characteristic belongs to PERT).

q: 4. The scheduling of project activities is dine in such a way that it consumes resources
options: greater at the start, lesser at the end
lesser at the start, greater at the end
explain: Good scheduling gives a uniform resource demand (levelling).

q: 5. Which of the following represent an activity?
explain: Construction of foundation, roof, and superstructure are all time- and resource-consuming tasks, hence all represent activities.

q: 6. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow
explain: Individual activity durations in PERT are assumed to follow a Beta distribution.

q: 7. In a barchart the vertical axis represents
explain: Activities are listed on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis.

q: 8. Negative slack occurs
options: when latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack indicates the project is behind schedule, often caused by resource shortages or delays.

q: 9. In the network shown in Fig., activity 4-5 can be started only when
explain: From the given network, node 4 is reached only after both activities 2-4 and 3-4 are complete, so activity 4-5 requires both to finish first.

q: 10. The barchart technique is commonly used because it
options: is simple to draw and easy to understand
is useful for cost and quality control
explain: Per the answer key, a. Its popularity comes from being simple to draw and understand.

q: 11. A stage or point where all previous jobs merging in it are completed and all further jobs bursting out are still to be completed is known as a
explain: This describes a node in the network, which is technically an event.

q: 12. The main function of the construction management is
explain: Management covers planning, organising, directing and controlling.

q: 13. Earliest finish time of an activity is always
options: equal to or more than earliest event time of the following node
equal to or less than earliest event time of the following node
more than earliest time of the following node
explain: Earliest finish time is equal to or less than the earliest event time of the following node[cite: 1].

q: 14. The latest allowable time for any event i is equal to
explain: To ensure no following activities are delayed, the latest allowable time is the minimum of the late finishes of succeeding activities minus their durations.

q: 15. Each work should be planned with respect to
options: manner of execution of the work
explain: Planning considers the execution method, urgency and resource availability.

q: 16. SLACK time refers to an
explain: Slack is specifically associated with events (the difference between $T_L$ and $T_E$), while 'float' is associated with activities.

q: 17. The technique which is activity oriented is
explain: CPM is activity-oriented, focusing on individual activities and their durations, unlike PERT which is event-oriented.

q: 18. The minimum number of years required to complete any research project may be
explain: Research projects have variable timelines depending on complexity and findings.

q: 19. Which one of the following represents an event?
explain: 'Concrete cured' represents a completed milestone/state (an event), while the others describe ongoing activities.

q: 20. Which of the following is an example of parallel activities?
options: Construction of walls and casting of roof
Construction of walls and carpentry work of doors and window
Casting of roof and construction of septic tank
Digging of well and construction of septic tank
explain: Per the answer key, b. Wall construction and door/window carpentry can proceed at the same time.

q: 21. An event is indicated on the network by a number enclosed in
explain: While circles are standard, various shapes like squares or ellipses can be used to represent nodes in different conventions.

q: 22. Which of the following is an activity
explain: Even though phrased in past tense, all listed processes (curing, plastering, excavation) originally represent work/tasks consuming time - so all of the above per the answer key.

q: 23. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its
explain: The completion event is the head event, at the arrowhead.

q: 24. Free float is mainly used to
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total of preceding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of either the preceding or succeeding activities
explain: Free float specifically identifies how much an activity can be delayed without affecting the float or start of the succeeding activity.

q: 25. The occurrence of the starting of an activity is called its
explain: The starting event is the tail event.

q: 26. The free float affects only
explain: Free float affects preceding activities/successor relationships as per definition[cite: 1].

q: 27. The area under the beta-curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time ($t_e$) is the mean of the distribution, which bisects the area under the probability curve.

q: 28. If the path of activities leads back into itself, the resulting error in the network is known as
explain: A closed cycle of activities is a loop (looping error).

q: 29. For a curve, larger the variance
explain: Variance is a measure of spread; a higher variance means the actual time could deviate significantly from the mean, increasing uncertainty.

options: the shortest time required to complete the activity under favorable conditions
the maximum time required to complete the activity under adverse conditions
the time the activity would most often require if normal conditions prevail
explain: Optimistic time is the shortest time if everything goes well.

explain: The 'E' in $t_E$ stands for 'Expected' time, which incorporates the uncertainty inherent in PERT.

q: 33. The activity which is crashed first has
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: Crashing follows a least-cost approach, starting with the critical activity having the least (lowest) cost slope to minimize the additional cost incurred.

q: 34. If t_o, t_p and t_L represent the optimistic, pessimistic and most likely time estimates, the expected time of completion of the activity is given by
explain: PERT (beta distribution) gives t_E = (t_o + 4t_L + t_p)/6.

explain: A node with multiple incoming arrows and one outgoing arrow represents a merge event[cite: 1].

q: 36. The probability distribution taken to represent the completion time in PERT analysis is
explain: PERT assumes activity times follow the beta distribution.

options: more than the number of activity
equal to the number of activity
explain: The relationship between the number of events and activities depends entirely on the network topology and the use of dummy activities.

41. Positive slack indicates
explain: Positive slack means there is extra time available, implying the project or event is ahead of its required deadline.

q: 42. In resource levelling
options: total duration of project is reduced
total duration of project is increased
uniform demand of resources is achieved
explain: Resource levelling aims to smooth out resource demand fluctuations over the project duration, achieving a more uniform resource requirement, potentially extending duration.

q: 43. The slack for an event i is given by
explain: Slack for an event is calculated as the Latest Allowable occurrence time ($T_L$) minus the Earliest Expected occurrence time ($T_E$).

q: 44. A dummy activity is that part of the project which
explain: A dummy activity has zero duration and consumes no resources; it exists only to maintain correct network logic.

q: 45. Variance is
options: Sum of time duration / number of jobs
difference between time and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviation
explain: Mathematically, variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean.

q: 46. In PERT analysis is the duration of the activities is taken as
explain: PERT uses the expected (mean) time, calculated from the three estimates, as the duration for each activity in scheduling calculations.

q: 47. The square root of the variance is known as
explain: By definition, the standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

q: 48. t^{ij} and t_E^{ij} indicates the time required for completion of an activity in CPM and PERT respectively. Here the subscript E stands for
explain: In PERT, subscript E denotes the expected time accounting for uncertainty[cite: 1].

q: 49. The variance will be zero if
explain: Variance is only zero if all data points (durations) are exactly equal to the mean.

q: 50. The variance of the PERT critical path is equal to
options: sum of variance of activities lying on critical path
maximum of sum of variances upto end event
minimum of sum of variances upto end event
explain: The variance of the project completion time equals the sum of the variances of all activities lying on the critical path.
